input.title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via 'customer' query parameter
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:15-16 registers GET /orders/search with no auth decorator, and the docstring at :17 says the storefront's public order lookup page uses it. At :18 the `customer` value comes straight from request.args, with no validation. At :20 it is put into the SQL string with an f-string inside single quotes, and :21 runs it on a sqlite3 connection (app/db.py:8-11). A request like `?customer=' OR '1'='1` breaks out of the quotes and returns every order row (id, total, status) for every customer. UNION-based payloads can also read other tables. sqlite3's execute() runs only one statement, which limits stacked queries but doesn't stop data being read. An unauthenticated attacker can reach this route.
input.recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,)). Also think about whether a public endpoint should return orders based only on an email address. That is an authorization/enumeration issue on its own, even once the injection is fixed. Add a regression test that sends a quote payload.

input.title: False positive: /reports/status builds SQL only from a hardcoded allowlist
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:28 reads the user-controlled `status` parameter into `key`. But at :29 `key` is used only as a lookup key in REPORT_STATUSES (:8-12), and any unknown value falls back to the constant "OPEN". So the `status` value put into the query at :31 can only be one of "OPEN", "SHIPPED" or "REFUNDED", all hardcoded constants. User input never reaches the SQL string.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix is needed. As a defensive cleanup, switch to a parameterized query (WHERE status = ?) so the code stays safe if the allowlist changes later and the scanner stops flagging it.

input.title: False positive: f-string SQL in test seed data uses constant values only
input.evidence: demo-store-api/tests/test_search.py:13 builds an INSERT with an f-string. The only values are the loop index `i` and `email` from SEED_EMAILS, a hardcoded list of constants (:7, :12). This is a test fixture (seed(), :10-14) that pytest calls on a temporary database (:18-20). It isn't part of the deployed app and takes no external input.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix is needed. Optionally use parameters (VALUES (?, ?, 10.0, 'OPEN')) for consistency, and exclude tests/ from this rule or suppress it there.

content.text:
I reviewed all three findings and saved a draft ticket for each. Only one is a real problem: an injectable search endpoint that anyone can call without logging in.

| ID | Location | Verdict | Severity | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-001 | app/main.py:20 | **Exploitable** | Critical | The `customer` value comes straight from the request (main.py:18) and is pasted into the SQL query (main.py:20) on a public, no-login endpoint (`/orders/search`, main.py:15-17). A request like `' OR '1'='1` returns every customer's orders, and other payloads can read other tables. |
| F-002 | app/main.py:31 | Not exploitable | None | The user's input is only used to look up a fixed list (main.py:8-12, 29), and unknown values fall back to `"OPEN"`. Only hardcoded values ever reach the query. |
| F-003 | tests/test_search.py:13 | Not exploitable | None | This is test setup code, and every value in the query is a hardcoded constant (test_search.py:7, 12). It isn't part of the running app. |

**Key points:**
- **F-001 is rated above the scanner's "high"** because no login is needed and it exposes all order data. The fix is a parameterized query (`WHERE customer_email = ?`). Even after that, letting anyone look up orders with just an email address is a separate data-exposure risk that should be addressed. The existing test (test_search.py:17-24) only sends a normal email, so a test that sends an injection payload should be added.
- **F-002 and F-003** need no security fix. Switching both to parameterized queries would keep them safe if the code changes later and stop the scanner flagging them.

All three drafts are waiting for human review before they're filed.
